completed_projects.description:
Make verification of the minimal core tree fast by selection, parallelism and timing data that already exist, and move the full battery from each task's close to each orchestration's close

WHY. Every phase of every remaining task on this branch that edits extensions/core/** verifies against the same 77-suite battery, and the only harness that exists, integration/tools/run-core-suite-three-roots.sh, runs all 77 suites three times with --jobs 1. It uses none of the narrowing and scheduling the runner it calls already ships.

MEASURED AT CREATION, CARRIED-UNVERIFIED, re-derive first (step 1 below exists for this):
- One three-root pass ran past 27 minutes on a 24-core host. That figure is contaminated: two copies of the harness were live, started 12 seconds apart by one implement dispatch, because the harness has no single-flight guard.
- extensions/core/scripts/tests/suite-cost-hints.txt puts the suites present in this tree at about 357s per root serial. Three suites are 67% of it: test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (107s), test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (68s), test-git-commit-scoped.sh (66s).
- extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh already accepts --only, --jobs N|auto, --timings FILE, --class, --tag, --cost-class and --fail-on-new. extensions/core/scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh already resolves touched paths to suite basenames (suite_selection_select, suite_selection_unmapped, suite_selection_classify) and returns the sentinel __FULL_SWEEP__ for a touched path with no mapped suite.

BINDING REQUIREMENT: USE WHAT EXISTS. The deliverables below are callers of run-all.sh's existing flags and of suite-selection-lib.sh's existing public API. Do not write a second selection engine, a second scheduler or a second timing format. Prefer new files under integration/tools/ over edits to extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh or extensions/core/scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh, which are copies of an upstream tree; any edit to a copied file is a local divergence and must be recorded beside the existing divergence notes in extensions/core/README.md.

DELIVERABLES.

1. Baseline. On an idle host with no other dispatch live, run each root once with --timings and record per-suite, per-root wall time plus nproc and loadavg. Every later speed claim is stated against this table. Refresh suite-cost-hints.txt from it if the checked-in figures are stale for this tree.

2. Touched-path inner loop: integration/tools/verify-touched.sh. Input is a set of paths (default: the working-tree and staged diff against a named base). It resolves them through suite_selection_select, then runs run-all.sh --only <resolved> --jobs auto --timings <file> under one root. It prints the resolved suite list, the paths that resolved to nothing, and the verdict. This is the per-phase check for every non-final and final phase of a task.

3. Unmapped paths stop meaning "run everything now". Today an unmapped touched path forces the whole battery, which makes the fast path collapse on exactly the edits (new files, docs, data files) that are most common. Replace that with a classified fallback, decided per path, never silently:
   (a) NO-SUITE-BY-CLASS: a path whose class cannot change suite behaviour (prose under a docs directory, a records file) runs the cheap lints that do read it and nothing else. The class list is a checked-in data file, each row carrying its reason.
   (b) EXPLICIT MAP ROW: a checked-in map file names the suites for paths the basename resolution misses (data files a suite reads, a library sourced by several subjects). Adding a row is the normal repair for an unmapped path.
   (c) OWED, NOT PAID: a path still unmapped after (a) and (b) runs a small declared fallback set now (select it with --cost-class or --class, do not hand-list suites) and writes a durable "full sweep owed" record that the orchestration-close battery in step 6 discharges. Owed is never forgiven: a close battery that did not run leaves the record open and visible.
   (d) A coverage report lists every file under extensions/core/** that resolves to no suite, no map row and no class, so the map is fixed once rather than paid for on every edit. Research decides whether a nonzero count fails or warns.

4. Root-sensitivity, derived rather than hand-tagged. Most suites cannot behave differently across SF1_DEPLOY_ROOT=.claude, SF1_DEPLOY_ROOT=.opencode and the isolated root; only the ones that read the deploy root or detect the tree layout can. Derive that subset mechanically from the suites' own text and their sourced libraries, and let verify-touched.sh run the root-sensitive members of its selection under all three roots and the rest under one.
   The guard on that derivation must NOT be a suite inside the battery it guards: a selection mechanism cannot be the thing that decides whether its own check runs. Two independent guards instead:
   - a standalone preflight the harness runs before any suite, outside run-all.sh's discovery, which fails the run when the derived classification is stale or a suite reads the deploy root without being classed sensitive;
   - an empirical cross-check at orchestration close: the close battery runs every suite under every root, and any suite classed root-invariant whose result differs between roots fails the battery and names itself. A wrong classification is therefore caught by measurement at every close, not only by a static rule.
   Apply the same "not inside what it guards" rule to the selection checks in general: identify which existing suites assert properties of selection itself and make sure the close battery, which is unfiltered, is where their verdict is authoritative.

5. The three-root harness itself. Run the three roots concurrently, each in its own scratch copy so they cannot collide on shared state, with --jobs auto inside each and --timings recorded per root. Add a single-flight guard so a second concurrent invocation waits for or joins the first rather than starting. Add a green cache keyed on a content hash of the tree under test so an unchanged tree returns the recorded result immediately. Keep an explicit --serial form that reproduces today's --jobs 1 behaviour byte for byte, for any done-condition that requires serial.

6. Orchestrations, not tasks, close on the full battery. The unfiltered three-root battery runs ONCE per /orchestrate invocation, after the last task's work, and not at any task's own final phase. A task's final phase closes on verify-touched.sh plus any "full sweep owed" record it leaves. This holds for a batch of one task as well as a batch of many. Concretely:
   - provide the close battery as one entry point (the step 5 harness in its unfiltered form) that also discharges every open "owed" record and runs the step 4 cross-check;
   - declare it as this repository's closing gate and declare verify-touched.sh as this repository's narrowing form, in whatever repository-level declaration surface the deployed agent system reads, so the batch gate stage and the dispatch-time deferral directive can find both;
   - write the rule into AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, consistent with CONTRIBUTING.md's existing merge gate (bash sf1-v2/run-tests.sh plus the suites the PR touches), so a planner stops declaring the full battery on a task's final phase;
   - INTERIM, until the deployed agent system can invoke a repository-declared closing gate by itself: document the one command the operator or the orchestrator runs after a batch, and make a batch that ended without it leave a visible open record.

7. Slow suites. Profile the three suites that dominate the baseline. They are copies of upstream suites, so the default disposition is to report the findings to the source store rather than diverge the copies; edit locally only where the gain is large and the divergence is recorded.

HARD CONSTRAINTS.
- Do not weaken coverage to buy speed. Every reduction in what runs at a given moment must be matched by a named later moment at which it does run. Nothing is excluded; things are deferred to the orchestration close and recorded.
- A subset pass is never reported as a full pass. verify-touched.sh's output and any record it writes say which suites ran and under which roots.
- No file under .claude/** is edited (it is a regenerated deploy artifact). Agent-system mechanism changes belong to the source store and are tracked there, not here.
- No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file outside specs/**.

CROSS-REPOSITORY EDGES (prose, not state edges; these records live in the agent-system source store at /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/specs/). The source store carries the general forms of steps 2, 3 and 6: a touched-path verification entry point with an owed-not-paid fallback, and the orchestration-close ownership of the full battery for every invocation shape including a batch of one, alongside existing records on fitting the battery under the foreground ceiling, on suite wall-clock cost, and on narrowing forms for project sources. This task must work without them: steps 1 to 5 and step 6's interim form need nothing from the source store. When they land and are redeployed, step 6's declaration is what they read.

DONE WHEN: the baseline table is recorded; verify-touched.sh is the documented per-phase check and demonstrably runs a strict subset for a single-file edit; an unmapped path produces a classified outcome and, where owed, a record the close battery discharges; the root-sensitivity preflight and the cross-root cross-check both exist and both fail on a seeded misclassification; the close battery runs three roots in parallel, refuses to double-start, and its measured idle wall time is recorded against the baseline; AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md state the per-phase and per-orchestration rules.

SOURCE-STORE DEPENDENCY NOTE (added 2026-11-18). The records named in CROSS-REPOSITORY EDGES above are, in /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/specs/state.json (that repository's numbering, not this one's): 650 touched_path_verify_entry_and_unmapped_fallback, 651 orchestration_close_owns_full_battery (which itself depends on 650 and 610), plus the existing 610, 599 and 586. They cannot be state edges here because they live in another repository.
- NOT a hard dependency: steps 1 to 5, step 7, and step 6's declaration, documentation and interim form can all be implemented and completed without 650 or 651 landing.
- SOFT dependency, step 6 only: the close battery running AUTOMATICALLY at the end of every /orchestrate, including a batch of one, with per-task final phases mechanically prevented from running it, needs 651 (and 599 for the repository-declared closing gate) implemented and redeployed into this checkout. Until then the interim one-command form is the delivered behaviour, and this task's summary must say which form is live.
- 650 is the general form of steps 2 and 3. If it lands and is redeployed before this task is implemented, call its entry point from integration/tools/ rather than writing verify-touched.sh's selection and fallback logic locally; if it lands after, record verify-touched.sh as the piece to retire in its favour.

The 29 are: test-assess-repo-health, test-deploy-baseline-lib, test-deploy-root-guard, test-force-phases, test-gate-lock, test-gate-out-derived-staleness, test-gate-out-repair-reporting, test-gate-out-self-attribution, test-generate-task-order, test-handoff-dispatch-identity, test-handoff-reader-parity, test-init-specs, test-orchestrate-build-dispatch, test-orchestrate-cycle-plan, test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight, test-orchestrate-recover-message-findings, test-orchestrate-suggest-next-batch, test-postflight-deploy-gate, test-reconcile-demote-stranded, test-reconcile-handoff-status, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion, test-resume-scan-nonconformance, test-routing-resolution, test-run-all-selection, test-stall-reprompt-wiring, test-status-vocabulary, test-task-type-detect, test-update-task-status, test-validate-artifact. Observed causes, to be verified suite by suite rather than trusted: source-store-mode resolution that still expects an `agent-system/extensions/core/` layout where this tree lives at `extensions/core/`; suites reading files the cut removed (`orchestrate-churn.sh`, `lib/gate-verdict-extract-lib.sh`, the redeploy checkpoint library); schemas and docs the copy list never carried (`state-schema.json`, `batch-admit-schema.md`); and routing assertions for extensions absent from a core-only tree. The copy task labelled 23 of these pre-existing because they also fail when run in place from `extensions/core/`; that is the same copied tree, not a control. The real control is the upstream source store, where these suites are expected to pass, and research must run it. Every failing suite gets exactly one recorded disposition: (a) copy the missing dependency into `extensions/core/` and add it to `core-file-manifest.txt` with its reachability reason; (b) repoint a layout or path assumption to the new tree and `SF1_DEPLOY_ROOT`; or (c) remove the suite from the tree and the manifest because its subject was deliberately cut, naming the cut. No assertion is weakened to make a suite pass, and no suite is left failing under an exclusion. Also in scope: roughly 30 further test fixtures that build a scratch sandbox with a hard-coded `.claude` directory name and inherit the outer `SF1_DEPLOY_ROOT`; six were patched by pinning the variable inside the fixture, and research must decide whether pinning is the right treatment or whether those fixtures should honour the variable, then apply one treatment to all of them. Done when `run-all.sh` is fully green under `.claude`, under `.opencode`, and under an isolated root containing only the new tree, run serially, with the per-suite disposition table checked in beside the manifest. Constraints: no edit under `.claude/**` or `integration/claude-system/`; the footprint budget pass must not start until this lands, since it edits the same tree and needs a green suite to verify its cuts Prior partial attempt: the copy task's implementation agent began disposition (b) and ran out of context before verifying or committing it. Those edits (78 files under `extensions/core/`, chiefly `agent-system/extensions/core` path literals repointed to `extensions/core`, plus a few new `HAVE_*` presence guards in test suites) were removed from the working tree and preserved at `specs/016_copy_minimal_core_tree_and_deploy_root_variable/working-progress-1795012345.patch`. Treat the patch as unreviewed input: the path repoints may be reusable, but each added presence guard must be checked against the no-weakened-assertion rule before any of it is applied
